html:
V. S. Naipaul was a novelist and travel writer born in Chaguanas, Trinidad, in 1932, to a family descended from indentured Indian labourers. He won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2001.

His novel A House for Mr Biswas (1961), based on his father, tells of an Indo-Trinidadian man's struggle for a home of his own. He left for Oxford at 18 and lived in England.

His later books on India, Africa and the Muslim world were sharp and often bleak, and many critics called his views of former colonies harsh. He remains, with Derek Walcott, the best known writer of the English Caribbean and a voice of its Indian community.
